title: SDK: gradual typing function hints + resilient stream wrappers and telemetry
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Implement a cross-language, opt-in ‘function hint’ layer and resilient streaming wrapper for the SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go). Goal: provide ergonomic runtime hints that enable lightweight validation, deterministic debug telemetry, and safe resumable streaming without forcing strict schema breakage for older clients. Deliverables: runtime hint API, example recipes, deterministic telemetry envelope, resumable stream checkpoint format, and adapter impls in Python/TS/Go.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose an opt-in 'function_hint' parameter allowing lightweight typing hints (primitives, shapes, array element types) that are used for local validation and coercion prior to network call
When hinting is enabled, SDK emits deterministic telemetry envelope (fn_call_id, hint_hash, coercions_applied, latency_ms, success/partial) to the existing telemetry pipeline
Streaming responses support resume tokens (stable opaque id) so interrupted streams can request a resume; TypeScript and Python wrappers implement resume logic, Go provides a minimal helper
Backward compatibility maintained: when no hints are provided SDK behavior identical to current invocation flow

Cross-SDK example recipes (Python/TS/Go) demonstrating: (a) hint usage to catch malformed args locally, (b) streaming resume after transient network drop, (c) telemetry trace linking to request and user-visible logs

implementation_notes: Approach: (1) Add 'function_hint' as an optional top-level parameter to the SDK call wrapper. Hints are small declarative maps (string -> basic type descriptors) used locally to validate/coerce. (2) Compute a short SHA256-based hint_hash for telemetry and cache evictions. (3) For streaming, wrap the generator/async-iterator with a checkpointing layer that emits checkpoints at sentence boundaries or user-configurable token windows. Checkpoint payloads are opaque to client but include fn_call_id + offset + hint_hash signed by SDK using per-client key to avoid tampering. (4) Provide ergonomic examples in each SDK rather than forcing a single contract format. Avoid shipping a heavy schema language; keep spec <= 1 A4.
risks: If backend resume semantics aren't finalized (ENG-61288), client resume may lead to duplicate partial outputs — mitigate by conservative defaults (resume=false) until server support verified
Hint coercion could mask user bugs if over-eager (e.g., silently cast string->number). Default to non-coercive mode; require explicit 'coerce=true' in hint options
Telemetry must avoid leakage of prompt content; only transmit hint_hash and coercion counts. Confirm with Privacy/Trust team before shipping telemetry change
qa_plan: Unit tests for hint validation/coercion matrix across types (python/ts/go)
Integration test simulating network drop mid-stream and asserting successful resume with identical output when server supports resumes
Property-based fuzz test: random hint vs payload pairs to ensure no panic/crash and predictable rejection behavior
End-to-end example app (chat playground) demonstrating hint-based local validation catching malformed user inputs before invocation
testing_examples: Go: NewHintBuilder().Field('query','[]string').Build() then client.InvokeWithHint(ctx, name, args, hint)
Resume example: start streaming, drop connection after checkpoint N, call resume(token) to continue and verify identical final output
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind 'fn_hints' on SDKs; default off for first week; enable for internal beta orgs
Staged rollout: internal + dogfood teams (72h) -> pilot customers (2 weeks) -> public by default (conditional on ENG-61288)
Monitoring: add dashboard for hint adoption rate, coercions_applied per 1000 calls, resume success rate, and errors per hint version
